:::{#def-set}
#### Set

A **set**
[@wikipedia_set_mathematics]
is a collection of distinct objects,
called its elements.
We write $a \in A$ when $a$ is an element of the set $A$,
and $a \notin A$ when it is not.
Two sets are equal when they have exactly the same elements.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-naive-set}
#### Naive and formal set theory

@def-set is the informal ("naive") notion of a set,
which is all these notes need.
Formal set theory states axioms for sets instead
[@wikipedia_set_mathematics].
For example, the last sentence of @def-set,
that two sets are equal when they have exactly the same elements,
is one of those axioms, the *axiom of extensionality*.

:::
